messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: P1 oncall -> Emily (oncall). Alert: elevated GPU ECC/corrected error rate + one unplanned host reboot on gpu-host-7 in us-west1. Linked metrics: <https://grafana.redwood/alerts/1802468135>. Pager: https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-12345 :rotating_light:
Emily (oncall): on it. grabbing logs + isolating host. starting timeline build here. pinging infra and cloud provider via partner channel.
Sanjay: how many pods affected? any customer-facing errors?
Emily (oncall): initial impact: ~3 in-flight inference hosts saw rpc timeouts -> 502s for a handful of sessions. Autoscaler retried some but we saw client retries spike. I flagged affected instances by instance label gpu-host-7 and gpu-host-8 (same host pool).
Lia: host gpu-host-7 shows an automatic reboot at 2026-03-15T14:02:17Z, kernel logs show PCIe AER events right before reboot. gpu-host-8 has corrected ECC counts spiking but not rebooted yet.
Chris: pasting relevant dmesg snippet:
```
[Mar 15 14:02:14] pcieport 0000:01:00.0: AER: Multiple Corrected error received: ID 00
[Mar 15 14:02:15] nvidia 0000:03:00.0: GPU HANG: page fault at 0x7f....
[Mar 15 14:02:16] nvidia_telemetry: ECC error detected on GPU0: corrected_count=124
[Mar 15 14:02:16] watchdog: watchdog0: watchdog did trigger reset
[Mar 15 14:02:17] kernel: Kernel panic - not syncing: GPU ECC fatal? -> rebooting
```
Ashley: thanks. hypothesis A: noisy neighbor causing PCIe AERs -> ECC counts increase -> driver triggers reset/watchdog. Hypothesis B: host firmware regression in vendor kernel causing spurious AERs.
ops-bot: metrics snapshot: latency p95 for text-generation route increased from 95ms -> 350ms between 14:00-14:05 UTC. error rate for hosted-api route increased from 0.3% -> 4%. Link: <https://grafana.redwood/d/rr/api-latency?from=2026-03-15T13:55:00Z&to=2026-03-15T14:10:00Z>
Sanjay: any customer impact posts? Which customers hit SLOs?
Emily (oncall): temporary error spikes for 6 customers, two reported user-facing failures (support ticket IDs: SUP-5598, SUP-5599). Redwood dedicated instances had isolation intact. Most affected were hosted placements on us-west1 cluster pool-a.
Lia: I'm starting live mitigation: cordon + drain gpu-host-8, mark gpu-host-7 as quarantined. Running: `kubectl cordon <node>` then `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data <node>`
Emily (oncall): executed drain on gpu-host-8 at 14:07Z. pods evicted; started provisioning replacements from pool-b. Observed successful failover for 90% of sessions; some long-lived sessions still timed out.
Chris: uploading full kernel logs and nvml logs to cloud storage: <https://storage.redwood/logs/incidents/1802468135/dmesg.log> and <https://storage.redwood/logs/incidents/1802468135/nvml.log>. Also attached a bow-tie of ECC counts per-GPU: <https://s3.redwood/graphs/1802468135/ecc-spike.png>
Emily (oncall): contacted cloud provider support (ticket CP-8764) and asked for host firmware & hypervisor logs. Provider acknowledges host-level maintenance pinged earlier but denies proactive reboots. asked them to check PCIe link errors and NIC firmware.
Ashley: while we wait, set fallback policy: route new requests from affected customers to model-variant quantized-v1 (lower mem footprint) to reduce KV cache churn. I pushed a temporary routing rule at 14:12Z.
Sanjay: good. owner for in-incident RCA doc? I'll own timeline + customer impact section. Lia will take host-level hypothesis and logs. Chris will collect driver/kernel evidence. Emily will own mitigation timeline + postmortem writeup.
Emily (oncall): agreed. creating incident doc: <https://wiki.redwood/incidents/1802468135-gpu-host-reboot-weird>. adding initial timeline:
- 13:58:56Z: trend of corrected ECC starts to climb on host pool-a
- 14:01:43Z: first increased RPC timeout alerts from hosted API
- 14:02:17Z: gpu-host-7 kernel-triggered reboot (AER events before reboot)
- 14:05:00Z: error rate peaks, customers start filing tickets
- 14:07:02Z: drain started on gpu-host-8
- 14:12:10Z: routing fallback to quantized-v1 enabled
- 14:20:00Z: error rates start returning toward baseline

Chris: small delta: also saw a live kernel oops referencing pcieport 0000:81:01.0 on a different host. may indicate vendor driver regression across host image.
Lia: next steps in-thread: 1) continue collecting nvml + firmware logs (Lia), 2) escalate with cloud provider to ask for host physical inspection / event logs (Emily), 3) schedule immediate rolling upgrade of host firmware on pool-a if provider confirms firmware bug (Sanjay+Infra), 4) expand ECC monitoring (alert at lower threshold) (Chris).
Emily (oncall): immediate action items assigned. I'll keep this thread updated. If anyone finds a smoking-gun (e.g., bad PCIe lanes, firmware changelog), paste here. Otherwise we'll draft RCA and schedule a follow-up war-room tomorrow 09:00 PT.
Ashley: add customer comms draft after we confirm root cause. propose: "We experienced degraded inference availability in us-west1 due to GPU host instability. We mitigated by draining impacted hosts and routing traffic to alternate capacity. We're investigating firmware/host-level causes and will follow up with a full RCA."
incident-bot: Incident P1 acknowledged by Emily. Handoff notes appended to incident: <https://pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-12345/notes> :white_check_mark:
Emily (oncall): handing off to morning oncall for continued tracking. marking postmortem owner Emily (oncall). closing paging for this shift.
